title: Texas's 19th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: This is an open-seat race for Texas's 19th Congressional District, a sprawling West Texas district anchored by Lubbock and Abilene. Incumbent Republican Rep. Jodey Arrington, who served since 2017 and chaired the House Budget Committee, announced his retirement in November 2025, triggering a competitive Republican primary. Republican nominee Tom Sell, an agriculture policy expert and former congressional aide, defeated conservative activist Abraham Enriquez in a May 26, 2026 runoff, while Democrat Kyle Rable, a PhD candidate and U.S. Army Reserve officer, secured the Democratic nomination. The district is heavily Republican — Donald Trump won it by 52 points in 2024 — making Sell the strong favorite in the general election.
polling_note: No specific general-election polls for Texas's 19th Congressional District were found as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Tom Sell
candidates.summary: Tom Sell is a fifth-generation West Texan, small business owner, and Republican nominee for Texas's 19th Congressional District. He co-founded the agriculture lobbying firm Combest, Sell & Associates, served as deputy chief of staff on the U.S. House Agriculture Committee for Rep. Larry Combest, and later served as Director of Intergovernmental Affairs at the USDA under President George W. Bush. Sell holds a BS in Agribusiness and a law degree from Texas Tech University and has emphasized conservative values, agriculture policy, and border security in his campaign.

candidates.name: Kyle Rable
candidates.summary: Kyle Rable is a PhD candidate in History at Texas Tech University, a U.S. Army Reserve Captain, and the Democratic nominee for Texas's 19th Congressional District. A former Secretary of the Lubbock County Democratic Party and a member of the Communications Workers of America Local 6186, Rable has centered his campaign on workers' rights, rural community revitalization, and protecting Medicaid, Medicare, and Social Security. He earned his undergraduate degree from the University of Toledo and a Master's from Bowling Green State University before moving to Lubbock for doctoral studies.

forecast.rationale: Texas's 19th Congressional District is a heavily Republican open seat with a structural partisan baseline that is overwhelmingly favorable to the GOP: Donald Trump carried the district by 52 points in 2024. No general-election polling exists for this race, which limits confidence and precludes overprecision. The Republican nominee, Tom Sell, is a well-credentialed former congressional aide and agriculture policy expert who defeated a conservative activist in a primary runoff. The Democratic nominee, Kyle Rable, is a PhD candidate and Army Reserve officer in a district that has not been competitive for Democrats at the presidential level. The open-seat context slightly tempers certainty versus an incumbent-held race, but the district's partisan fundamentals still indicate an overwhelming Republican advantage. The forecast is rated safe_r with medium confidence due to the lack of polling data.
